title: MVP
text: “Now then, materials!”
“You’re only just arriving and saying this?”
“Father and I prioritized guiding the evacuation, leaving the attacking to Kuro-chan and Father’s subordinates. Surely we’re entitled to a share, are we not?”
“That’s right. I think I fought reasonably well, don’t you?”
“Vau!”
The mongrel lizardman and Wolf declared to Itsuki. Even Itsuki couldn’t muster a face to deny it.
“Ah… well, I suppose that’s true. But what’s the point of a hero if he doesn’t take the lead?”
Incidentally, Ren seemed to have no room to join the conversation, too busy enduring the urge to vomit.
“I prioritized rescuing our precious Filolial-sama, indeed. Besides, isn’t finishing it off this quickly more than sufficient?”

It was practically a speedrun—I’d taken down the dimension chimera without overdoing the firepower. If I’d gone all out, a Brionac or a Liberation Prominence would’ve ended it in an instant. But since we needed the chimera’s and the monsters’ flesh, we’d agreed to secure as much as possible.
“…Very well. How shall we divide it up?”
“Ren wants the dragon head, doesn’t he?”
“Ah, yeah… uugh.”
Somehow holding back the urge to retch, Ren nodded.
“Then Itsuki, which part would you like?”
“…I’ll say the lion’s head.”
“Understood. Then Father and I will take the remaining head and the tail. Everything else gets split evenly, I say.”
“No objections.”
Ren nodded silently, over and over.
“Well then, let’s carry it, indeed.”
“I just carry this, right?”
“Wow.”
The mongrel lizardman and Wolf, having heard the plan, reached out to carry the goat head and snake tail that had fallen.
“Kou will carry too—”
“Kuro is watching Shadow Saint—”
“Very well, indeed.”
“Go home… seriously, go home…”

Ren seemed to be muttering something like a curse, but that was probably just my imagination. He couldn’t possibly be that displeased, surely. And so, we made our way back the way we’d come to report to Father.
“…This power. If only I’d had it back then.”

The mongrel lizardman murmured to itself. Regret comes in endless supply. Even I sometimes wish I’d had my current strength when I faced Spirit Tortoise, but if I hadn’t stumbled then, I never would have realized Fīro-tan’s true feelings, so it was an important thing, indeed. Truly, no matter how many regrets pile up, one should think of them later as things that were necessary. They are precious fragments that shape who I am today, after all.
“We’re back.”
“Welcome back— is that the spoils?”
“Indeed. The headline trophies. The rest comes later.”
Though I say that, I’d actually secured a bit of the chimera meat on the side. Just in case.
“A tribute for you, Father, indeed.”
The goat head and snake tail.
“What about you, Motoyasu-kun?”
“I already possess both, indeed.”
Since I’d unlocked the chimera itself somewhere along the way in battle already.
“Is that all right, then? Well, I’ll gratefully accept.”

Father absorbed the materials he’d brought back into his shield. This expanded the range of Father’s shield transformations. Considering the battles that might lie ahead for him, a shield born from the snake’s tail seemed like a genuinely useful item. As for the enhancement materials, since I’d been secretly stockpiling them, he’d be able to strengthen it right away.
“Anyway, somehow we managed to get through the wave.”
“It sounds like an overwhelming victory. It ended far more easily than what I’d heard.”
“…The last wave was hellish. Not something that should end this easily. Having heroes around must really make that much of a difference…”
The mongrel lizardman looked toward the untouched village, muttering with a complicated expression.
“Is that… relief? Or…”
“Envy. But it’s also true I’m glad there was no damage. Please don’t press on this matter further.”

In response to Rabbit Guy’s question, the mongrel lizardman glanced toward Father, bowed slightly, and answered. Oh? There seemed to be a demi-human mixed among the rescued villagers. Come to think of it, I’d heard that in the first world, a soldier had volunteered under Father and participated in the second wave, and that a demi-human had been mixed in among that soldier’s comrades. Now that I thought about it, indeed, in the now-peaceful village, that demi-human had occasionally been among the soldiers Father interacted with. In any case, that demi-human was now approaching the mongrel lizardman, calling out to it. The mongrel lizardman seemed to recognize the demi-human, and the two began talking.
“We did it!”
But my attention was drawn elsewhere, as Yuki-chan and the others came to report. Father, Fīro-tan, and Filolial-sama came first, after all.
“Was anyone hurt—?”

Seeing Yuki-chan and the others looking so proud, I couldn’t help but smile too. The damage was a complete zero. Even without me finishing things off in one decisive stroke, we could still achieve zero casualties. A perfect victory even with some restrictions in place… a splendid result, indeed.
“The Boss MVP was Kuro-chan, indeed. The Evacuation Guidance MVP was Yuki-chan. The Protection MVP was Kou—”
I went around praising every single Filolial-sama who had participated.
“““Yaaay!”””
“Big broooother!”
At that moment, Keel came running up alongside Elephant and the others.
“Is it already over?”
“Yep.”
“Figured, since the sky turned blue and all, but man, that really was crazy fast.”
“Was anyone injured?”
Elephant asked Father while checking on the state of the village.
“Nope. Everyone’s fine. We finished before the soldiers even arrived. Shion, Wolf, everyone did great.”
“I did great too!”
“Yes, yes. You too, Theo.”
“Bu… bubu.”
“Elena-san, please don’t try to hurry home and go to sleep, all right? Your job’s only just beginning, isn’t it?”

Lazy Pig really was lazy, I say! How exactly should one go about driving it out completely, the way I did when I had the Crimson Swine ingest Ouroboros Deadly Poison? Perhaps if I let it sense that I’d already dealt with the Crimson Swine and then threatened that it was next, that would do the trick?
“Everyone’s gotten stronger.”
Elephant nodded, as if fully aware that what came next mattered most.
“Well then, Keel-san, let’s head back.”
“Ehh… already going home?”
“Not going home? Then how about a walk with Luna and Keel?”
When Luna-chan, carrying Keel, made the suggestion, Keel glanced toward the direction of the castle town.
“All right! Back to the tent. See ya!”
“The kingdom’s soldiers are glaring at us, so if you’ll excuse us.”

And with that, Keel, Elephant, and Luna-chan hurried off. They were being treated as volunteer soldiers, after all. Still… there really were few soldiers who’d come as reinforcements. Someone ought to hurry up and reinforce the ranks, I say. As we were discussing such things, a well-dressed soldier—likely the next knight commander—who had gone over to speak with Ren and Itsuki, made a loud proclamation.
“Well done, heroes. The King has prepared a banquet for the party of heroes who overcame this wave. Rewards will also be given, so please come.”

That reminded me of what Father had said—that even if you cut off one head, another grows back. That arrogant expression, though belonging to a different person, told me the same rotten spirit persisted. Summoning us just to harass us, and going to all this trouble to do it—quite the effort, I say.
“Well… what should we do. Is it fine if I skip it?”
Since Father wasn’t hurting for money and had no need to retrace the loop, declining was certainly an option.
“Achieving such a feat and departing without giving your name—how truly like something out of a story!”
Rabbit Guy agreed with Father’s suggestion, practically buzzing with excitement.
“Sounds like it’d be a hassle. Well, though it might also feel a bit satisfying.”
Father had already been informed of what was to come.
“…Forgive me, but I have some interest in this castle banquet. Would it be all right if I went to observe?”
Here, the mongrel lizardman made this proposal to Father.
“Is that a request?”
“…Yes.”
In answer to Father’s question, the mongrel lizardman nodded. Rabbit Guy eyed the mongrel lizardman with a look of suspicion.
